guidelines.detail: refines ACT-05 (The description identifies submission as performed work, while the schema error shows a message event definition in an element that does not allow it. This clarifies how to apply the task-versus-event distinction in ACT-05.)

same as LRN-008 (The description places the waiter’s preparation alongside the kitchen and sommelier’s work, and the missing-element and missing-flow records show that this concurrent activity and its path to the synchronization point were omitted. This is already covered by learned guideline LRN-008.)

refines ACT-07 (The description places cart preparation alongside kitchen and sommelier work, with delivery dependent on readiness. The cart activity appears as a generated task (X5) despite the missing-element record (M1), so this does not establish that the activity itself was omitted. This guideline makes the concurrency and synchronization requirement explicit, refining ACT-07.)

same as LRN-031 (The description explicitly says the activity happens while other work is underway, and the later delivery depends on the food, wine, and cart being ready. The activity and its sequence flows are absent from the generated model. This is essentially the case already covered by LRN-031.)

same as LRN-032 (The task label pairs omit stated performers from several activity labels, while the description identifies those performers. This is already captured by learned guideline LRN-032. The end-event label difference does not support this task-label guideline.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a participant performs work by sending information to another participant: Model the sending as a task (use a send task when sending is itself the unit of work). Represent communication separately where appropriate; do not attach a message event definition to a task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant performs work by sending information to another participant

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies multiple independent activities that must all be completed before a later activity can begin: model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize them with a parallel join before the later activity
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an activity occurs while other independent activities are underway, and a later activity depends on all of them being complete

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes a participant’s instruction or assignment from the work that another participant is asked to perform: Label the BPMN activity as the instruction or assignment, preserving who directs whom; do not label it as though the directing participant were ordering or performing the requested work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes a participant’s instruction or assignment from the work that another participant is asked to perform

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a distinct activity is performed while other activities are in progress and that a later activity depends on their completion: Model the distinct activity and the other required work on concurrent branches, then synchronize those branches before the dependent activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a distinct activity is performed while other activities are in progress and that a later activity depends on their completion

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly identifies who performs an activity: Use a concise BPMN activity label that preserves the stated performer as well as the action, when needed to distinguish whose action it is.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly identifies who performs an activity
